THE TRAIL — the chosen direction, now drawn as a path through the piney woods.

The ribbon is much more pronounced than the first build: a 46px band with a full S-curve meander, waypoints sitting on it rather than beside it, and a leader line out to each row.

The copy is untouched — same six rows, same wording, same destinations as the live page.

THE PINES are drawn to match the daily-life illustration already on the page: loblolly form (tall bare trunks, high open crowns, drooping branch layers), the same sage and olive greens, warm grey-brown trunks, soft edges and fine needle texture.

They are vector, so they cost nothing in page weight and stay crisp at any size. Scale and opacity vary per tree to give the wood depth — nearer trees larger and stronger, further ones smaller and paler.

Both ends of the ribbon fade rather than stopping dead, so the path reads as continuing past the section. The pines fade at the foot for the same reason.

On mobile the trail keeps its meander at a narrower gauge and the pines sit to its left, mostly behind — the wood is suggested rather than spelled out, because there is no room to spell it out at 390px.

B — FINISH THE SENTENCE

Not chosen. Kept for the record: the visitor completes a sentence about themselves and the panel beneath swaps. The chips work — click them.

C — TWO WAYS IN

Not chosen. Kept for the record: the page forks into living-this and helping-build-it. Still the clearest of the three for major donors, if that ever becomes the priority.
